as_of_rule: oldest GetItem read date over the identifiers used
words: DB-b-286 (round 148, workstream CLASS, worker 0.9.0_WK_IRPT_DASHBD~230) changes account_class_daily.py and its class contract. ClassTable takes an injectable clock (default: the UTC run-day) and stamps every GetItem it makes, an absent item included, in read_dates; a cached lookup neither re-stamps nor re-reads. ClassTable.as_of(identifiers=None) answers the oldest stamp over the identifiers read, or None when none was read. emit_class_day takes classification_as_of and writes class_source.as_of and class_source.claim (held) into the day's manifest; the earlier class_source keys are unchanged. The class contract is 0.1.1 and gains exactly as_of and claim in class_source. The eight pure functions keep their exact source. The handler's one emit_classes call passes acd.default_table().as_of(). The new test file holds thirteen passing tests: six sum-to-account tests with the account values given independently and a sub-cent residual, each run alone against the four class_contribution mutants, and seven dating tests. Not proven: that the deployed function writes the date, which is a later code-update pair; that any reader reads it; and that default_table() is the table class_days reads at run time, which it is not (class_days builds a fresh ClassTable), so the handler's as_of is None until the wiring is ruled (surprise row IRPT_DASHBD-D2-W230-S1).
